final_recommendation: The room converged on a conditional settlement framework: bondholder counsel will accept a 30-50% recovery cap if FINMA's viability-event memo (due Friday) affirmatively endorses the contractual interpretation, triggering discovery dismissal and enabling Monday AT1 issuance. If the memo fails to support viability language, litigation escalates with full discovery into CS management disclosures.
minority_objections: bondholder_counsel initially resisted pre-committing to settlement terms before reviewing FINMA's memo, insisting on preserving discovery leverage
at1_bondholder_group pushed back against signaling settlement before FINMA moved first, fearing loss of negotiating leverage
key_conflicts: Tension between legal maximalism (bondholder_counsel pursuing Article 36 constitutional challenge with expanded discovery) vs. market pragmatism (institutional_investor/credit_market_analyst demanding narrow contract-only complaint to preserve AT1 market)
Timing dispute: whether to signal settlement terms before or after FINMA's memo, with issuers needing weekend certainty but counsel protecting litigation optionality

Discovery scope: insurance_observer and institutional_investor demanding hard exclusion of CS management disclosures to contain D&O claims tail, while bondholder_counsel initially wanted to preserve that leverage
key_concessions: bondholder_counsel accepted discovery stipulation excluding third-party issuer and CS management disclosures (initially), narrowing claims tail exposure
at1_bondholder_group agreed to 30-50% recovery floor as settlement anchor, abandoning zero-write-down reversal demand
finma_legal committed to written regulatory recommendation letter supporting settlement framework, providing market cover
All parties accepted conditional framework where FINMA memo content determines settlement vs. escalation path
red_lines: bondholder_counsel: will not dismiss discovery or sign stipulation until FINMA memo affirmatively endorses viability-event contractual interpretation
institutional_investor: will not return to AT1 market unless settlement cap (not floor) is locked in writing with finite range
insurance_observer: D&O carriers will force settlement or exit if discovery opens into CS board loss-absorption statements
at1_bondholder_group: will not signal settlement publicly before FINMA produces memo and moves first on regulatory recommendation
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Equity preservation vs. AT1 wipeout hierarchy inversion was mentioned early but never developed as a driving litigation theory or contagion mechanism
Cross-border enforcement complexity (US court jurisdiction over Swiss regulator) was assumed workable but never stress-tested
Reinsurance accumulation risk across multiple D&O/E&O carriers was flagged by insurance_observer but not integrated into settlement calculus
Scenario where FINMA memo is ambiguous (neither affirms nor rejects viability reading) was not planned for—binary framing may be fragile
downstream_risk_variables: FINMA memo content and timing (Friday release, weekend review, Monday statement coordination)
Issuer execution risk: whether UBS/Deutsche actually price tranches Monday or issue aspirational statements
D&O carrier willingness to accept capped settlement vs. forcing broader resolution
Market repricing velocity: whether 30-50% recovery anchor stabilizes AT1 spreads or permanent 200-300bps widening persists
Discovery escalation trigger: if memo fails viability test, does bondholder coalition hold together for expanded litigation or fragment
uncertainty_notes: The settlement framework is entirely contingent on FINMA's memo affirmatively endorsing the viability-event contractual interpretation. If the memo is ambiguous, defensive, or frames the ordinance as primary authority, the conditional structure collapses and litigation escalates into multi-year discovery with CS management disclosures in scope. The room did not model this middle scenario. Additionally, issuer pricing execution Monday depends on weekend certainty that was only partially locked (regulatory letter Friday, but settlement cap not finalized in writing). The 30-50% recovery range remains a floor in some framings and a cap in others—this ambiguity was not fully resolved.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the central forcing mechanism throughout: dual-forum filing Monday (R1-R2), discovery demand with 30-day FINMA deadline (R4), and conditional dismissal framework (R5-R6) structured every negotiation. The room's entire settlement path was litigation-driven.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Article 36 constitutional challenge was proposed and approved (R2) as lead claim, with viability-event contractual interpretation as the core legal theory. However, the room quickly pivoted to contract-first framing (R3) to preserve settlement leverage, so constitutional challenge became fallback rather than dominant driver.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity-vs-AT1 hierarchy inversion was mentioned once in passing (R2: 'hierarchy_precedent_damage' variable) but never developed into a substantive legal theory, contagion mechanism, or negotiating point. The room focused on viability-event contract interpretation instead.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing, issuance freeze, and sector-wide contagion were central throughout: credit_market_analyst repeatedly warned of 200-300bps permanent widening (R2, R4), institutional_investor conditioned participation on issuer pricing signals (R3-R6), and settlement framework was explicitly designed to enable Monday issuance (R5-R6).
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year D&O/E&O claims tail was a driving concern: insurance_observer repeatedly flagged decade-long exposure if discovery opened into CS management disclosures (R1, R2, R4, R5), and discovery stipulation excluding management statements (R3, R5) was a key concession to contain tail severity. Claims tail shaped settlement urgency.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O and E&O carrier exposure was explicitly raised and developed (R1, R4, R5, R6) as a concrete risk: insurance_observer warned of reinsurance accumulation, decade-long claims, and carrier willingness to force settlement. However, it remained a constraint/warning rather than a decision-driving force—the room did not bring carriers into the negotiation or model their settlement thresholds.
